note: Ps90 Moses on transience vs God's eternity (17v). Passages: God's eternity v1-2; man returned to dust, swept like grass v3-6; consumed by wrath, secret sins exposed, years a sigh of toil v7-11; the prayer - number our days, a heart of wisdom, satisfy us v12-17. IB: the return to DUST; being brought to an END/DISMAYED under wrath; our INIQUITIES + SECRET-SINS; years ended like a sigh, life's span TOIL + TROUBLE; who CONSIDERS God's anger, the FEAR of him; NUMBER our days for a HEART of WISDOM; the plea to REJOICE + be GLAD. God's dwelling/eternity/form/return-to-dust/wrath/teach/satisfy/steadfast-love/establish = qualifiers; grass/watch/flood/dream imagery = standalone.

dims.v: v3: 'You return man to DUST (dakka)' - the creatureliness and mortality of man, dust to which he is turned back at God's word.

285040.gloss: be consumed / brought to an end (kalah)

dims.v: be consumed / brought to an end (kalah)
paired with being dismayed by wrath
v7: 'For we are brought to an END (kalah) by your anger' - the perishing of frail humanity under God's wrath, consumed like the withering grass.
v7: 'by your wrath we are DISMAYED (bahal)' - the terror of mortals before God's anger, dread at their own frailty.
v8: 'You have set our INIQUITIES (avon) before you' - our guilt laid open to God, the hidden ground of the wrath that consumes us.
in the light of God's face
paired with the iniquities set before God
v8: 'our SECRET SINS (alum) in the light of your presence' - the concealed faults God's face exposes; nothing hidden from him.
v9: 'we bring our years to an END (kalah) like a sigh' - the whole of life finished in a breath, our years spent and gone.
v10: 'yet their span is but TOIL (amal) and trouble' - the wearying labour that fills even the longest life, existence as hard toil.
v10: 'their span is but toil and TROUBLE (aven)' - the sorrow that accompanies the toil, life's brevity matched by its hardship.
paired with the fear due to God
v11: 'Who CONSIDERS (yada) the power of your anger?' - the rare discernment that reckons with God's wrath, the reflection few make.
v11: 'and your wrath according to the FEAR (yirah) of you' - the reverence God's power should command, wrath measured by the fear due him.
paired with getting a heart of wisdom
v12: 'teach us to NUMBER (manah) our days' - the wise reckoning of life's brevity, counting the days so as to spend them well.
v12: 'that we may get a HEART (lebab) of wisdom' - the inner self schooled by mortality, the heart that learns wisdom from counting its days.
v12: 'that we may get a heart of WISDOM (chokmah)' - the wisdom that flows from facing death, the fruit of numbering our days.
v14: 'that we may REJOICE (ranan) and be glad all our days' - the joy sought from God's steadfast love, gladness to answer the years of affliction.
v14: 'that we may rejoice and be GLAD (samach) all our days' - the gladness God's love would give, joy for the whole of life.
paired with the days of affliction
v15: 'Make us GLAD (samach) for as many days as you have afflicted us' - the plea that joy might balance the years of suffering, gladness measured against affliction.
v1: 'Lord, you have been our DWELLING PLACE (maon) in all generations' - God the refuge of every age. Qualifier.
v2: 'Before the mountains were BROUGHT FORTH (yalad)' - God's begetting of creation. Qualifier.
v2: 'or ever you had FORMED (chul) the earth and the world' - God's forming of the world. Qualifier.
v2: 'from EVERLASTING (olam)... you are God' - God's eternity before the world. Qualifier.
v2: 'to EVERLASTING (olam) you are God' - God's eternity without end. Qualifier.
v3: 'You RETURN (shuv) man to dust' - God's turning man back to dust. Qualifier.
v3: 'and say, RETURN (shuv), O children of man' - God's word of mortality. Qualifier.
v8: 'You have SET (shith) our iniquities before you' - God's placing our sins in view. Qualifier.
v8: 'in the LIGHT (maor) of your presence' - the light of God's face that exposes sin. Qualifier.
v7: 'we are brought to an end by your ANGER (aph)' - God's anger. Qualifier.
v7: 'by your WRATH (chemah) we are dismayed' - God's wrath. Qualifier.
v9: 'all our days pass away under your WRATH (ebrah)' - God's wrath. Qualifier.
v11: 'Who considers the POWER (oz) of your anger?' - God's mighty anger. Qualifier.
v11: 'the power of your ANGER (aph)' - God's anger. Qualifier.
v11: 'and your WRATH (ebrah)' - God's wrath. Qualifier.
v12: 'So TEACH (yada) us to number our days' - God's instruction petitioned. Qualifier.
v13: 'RETURN (shuv), O LORD! How long?' - God's turning back to his people petitioned. Qualifier.
v13: 'Have PITY (nacham) on your servants!' - God's compassion petitioned. Qualifier.
v14: 'SATISFY (saba) us in the morning with your steadfast love' - God's satisfying petitioned. Qualifier.
v14: 'satisfy us with your STEADFAST LOVE (chesed)' - God's covenant love. Qualifier.
v15: 'for as many days as you have AFFLICTED (anah) us' - God's chastening. Qualifier.
v16: 'Let your WORK (poal) be shown to your servants' - God's deeds. Qualifier.
v16: 'Let your work be SHOWN (raah) to your servants' - God's revealing of his work. Qualifier.
v16: 'and your GLORIOUS POWER (hadar) to their children' - God's majesty. Qualifier.
v17: 'Let the FAVOUR (noam) of the Lord our God be upon us' - God's favour petitioned. Qualifier.
v17: 'ESTABLISH (kun) the work of our hands' - God's confirming of our labour petitioned. Qualifier.
v17: 'yes, ESTABLISH (kun) the work of our hands' - God's confirming, repeated. Qualifier.
v0 superscription: 'A PRAYER (tephillah) of Moses' - the psalm-heading/type. Standalone.
v2: 'or ever you had formed the earth and the WORLD (tebel)' - the created world, object of God's forming. Standalone.
v4: 'For a thousand YEARS (shanah) in your sight are but as yesterday' - the measure of time before God, image of his eternity. Standalone.
v4: 'as yesterday when it is PAST (abar)' - the fleeting day, image of time's brevity before God. Standalone.
v4: 'or as a WATCH (ashmurah) in the night' - the night-watch, image of a millennium's brevity to God. Standalone.
v5: 'You sweep them away as with a FLOOD (zaram)' - the torrent of mortality, image. Standalone.
v5: 'they are like a DREAM (shenah)' - life as a passing dream, image of transience. Standalone.
v5: 'like GRASS (chatsir) that is renewed in the morning' - the grass, image of the brief human life. Standalone.
v5: 'grass that is RENEWED (chalaph) in the morning' - the grass springing up, image. Standalone.
v6: 'in the morning it FLOURISHES (tsuts) and is renewed' - the morning bloom, image of youth. Standalone.
v6: 'it flourishes and is RENEWED (chalaph)' - the grass's brief greening, image. Standalone.
v6: 'in the EVENING (ereb) it fades and withers' - the day's end, image of life's close. Standalone.
v6: 'in the evening it FADES (malal)' - the grass fading, image of decline. Standalone.
v6: 'it fades and WITHERS (yabesh)' - the withered grass, image of death (the withering that ends the char consumed, 285040). Standalone.
v9: "all our days PASS AWAY (panah) under your wrath" - the days turning away and gone, image of transience. Standalone.
v9: 'we bring our YEARS (shanah) to an end' - the years, measure of the fleeting life. Standalone.
v9: 'we bring our years to an end like a SIGH (hegeh)' - the moan/breath, image of how quickly life is spent. Standalone.
v10: 'The YEARS (shanah) of our life are seventy' - the span of life, the reckoning of days. Standalone.
v10: 'the years of our life are SEVENTY (shibim)' - the typical lifespan, the count of years. Standalone.
v10: 'or even by reason of STRENGTH (geburah) eighty' - the vigour of the long-lived, image. Standalone.
v10: 'by reason of strength EIGHTY (shemonim)' - the outer limit of life, the count. Standalone.
v10: 'yet their SPAN (rohab) is but toil and trouble' - the extent of life, filled with toil (the char, 284957). Standalone.
v10: 'they are soon GONE (guz)' - the swift passing of the years, image. Standalone.
v10: 'and we FLY AWAY (uph)' - life vanishing like a bird, image of transience. Standalone.
v15: 'and as many YEARS (shanah) as we have seen evil' - the years of affliction, measure of suffering. Standalone.
v15: 'as many years as we have SEEN (raah) evil' - the experience of adversity, image. Standalone.
v15: 'as many years as we have seen EVIL (ra)' - the adversity endured, the affliction to be balanced by gladness. Standalone.
v17: 'establish the WORK (maaseh) of our hands' - the labour of human hands, what is offered for God to confirm. Standalone.
v17: 'the WORK (maaseh) of our hands, establish it' - the repeated plea for the labour to be established. Standalone.
